title: The countable-path proposition needs a nonempty path family.
details: Miller, Lecture notes in Computability Theory, December3,2008, §46 Proposition46.4, p.137, visually checked on2026-11-08. The statement assumes only that T is a computable binary tree and [T] is countable, then concludes that some computable branch belongs to [T]. Take T consisting only of the empty word: it is a computable nonempty prefix-closed tree and [T] is empty, hence countable, but it has no branch. Add [T] nonempty, or equivalently require an infinite binary tree as well as the countable path-family hypothesis. With that premise, an isolated path exists in the countable closed family and the stated finite-level search computes it. Only the missing hypothesis is recorded; no full perfect-subtree proof audit is claimed. This adjacent proposition is not selected for a new entry; the later low-basis theorem already assumes infinitude.
